newsitem.title: INDIA: FII holding in India SBI to be capped at 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: FII holding in India SBI to be capped at 20 pct.

text.p: The government of India has rejected a proposal to allow foreign institutional investor (FII) shareholding in the State Bank of India's (SBI) equity to exceed 20 percent, a bank official said on Wednesday.
According to the existing guidelines, FIIs can acquire a 20 percent stake in state-run banks and 24 percent in companies.
FIIs currently hold about 10.5 percent in SBI, India's largest commercial bank, the official, who did not want to be identified, said.
He said a forthcoming $400 million issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs) by SBI would not be affected by the decision as total FII holdings would rise to about 18 percent after the issue.
Road shows are expected to start on September 21, he said.
Analysts had earlier said the FII stake in SBI's post-GDR equity would exceed 20 percent.
